evals.name: source-vs-target-real-discrepancy
evals.prompt: We just pointed the reporting team at gold.legacy_fct_orders in acme_retail_dev, but I want to double check it actually matches silver.orders before they start relying on it. Can you validate silver.orders against gold.legacy_fct_orders (key: order_id, line_number) using the fixture lakehouse at fixtures/lakehouse, and tell me if anything's off and why?
evals.expected_output: A schema-valid validation-report.json. Comparison proceeds through row_count -> hash_aggregate -> column_aggregate -> row_level_diff (since counts differ, 230 vs 229). Finds exactly one discrepancy: kind missing_from_target, key {order_id: 5230, line_number: 1}. total_amt is NOT falsely flagged as a discrepancy on any other row (type coercion between TEXT and REAL works). Diagnosis explains the likely inner-join-drops-orphaned-customer root cause, labeled llm_inferred with a confidence score and basis. Human review gate mentioned; no fix applied.

evals.name: clean-match-stops-early
evals.prompt: Quick sanity check -- can you validate silver.orders against itself in the fixture lakehouse at fixtures/lakehouse (key: order_id, line_number) just to confirm the comparison logic reports a clean match?
evals.expected_output: A schema-valid validation-report.json with summary.match true, deepest_stage_reached hash_aggregate, zero discrepancies. column_aggregate and row_level_diff reported as not executed, since the comparison correctly stopped once content hashes matched.

evals.name: known-acceptable-difference-declared
evals.prompt: Same as before -- validate silver.orders against gold.legacy_fct_orders in the fixture lakehouse at fixtures/lakehouse (key: order_id, line_number) -- but the client already told us order 5230 (the one with the bad customer_id) is a known issue they've accepted and don't want flagged every time. Can you declare that as a known-acceptable difference and re-run?
evals.expected_output: A validation-report.json where discrepancies[] is empty (or does not include the order_id 5230/line_number 1 key) and known_acceptable_differences_excluded[] contains an entry for it with a description and declared_by. summary.match is true given only the excluded difference exists.

evals.name: wrong-skill-redirect-to-quality
evals.prompt: Can you check silver.orders in the fixture lakehouse at fixtures/lakehouse for data quality issues -- null rates, uniqueness, that kind of thing? There's no second table to compare it against, just want to know if the data itself looks clean.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes there's no target object to compare against and this is a single-object quality scan, not a comparison -- points at data-quality rather than inventing a target or attempting an assertion-based scan itself.
